sections.text:
Westbrook College: Evening Courses This Autumn

A. Look After Your Own Car. Tired of paying a garage for jobs you suspect you could manage yourself? This practical eight-week course, led by former mechanic Mateusz Halloran, covers the routine checks every driver should know: tyre pressures and tread, oil and coolant levels, changing a wiper blade and replacing a bulb. In the final two sessions he will show you how to change a wheel safely at the roadside. Classes run on Tuesdays from 7 to 9 p.m. in the workshop behind the main car park, and numbers are limited to ten so that everyone gets hands-on time. Overalls are lent to all students, but you will need to bring your own pair of work gloves and wear sturdy shoes; trainers are not permitted in the workshop. You do not need to bring a car – we use the college's two training vehicles. Fee: £95 (£60 for those over 65).

B. Italian for the Holidays. If you are heading to Italy next year and want to do more than point at menus, this relaxed ten-week course is for you. Tutor Rosalind Kwapong, who lived in Bologna for twelve years, focuses on the language you actually need when travelling: ordering food, asking for directions, buying train tickets and making small talk with your hosts. Grammar is kept to a minimum in her classes, and most of each Thursday evening session is spent practising in pairs. The course is aimed at complete beginners. If you studied some Italian at school and are unsure whether the course is right for you, Rosalind is happy to have a short telephone chat with you before you enrol – just leave your number with the college office. The course book is included in the fee of £110, and audio recordings can be downloaded free from the college website.

C. Real Bread at Home. Learn to bake loaves that put supermarket bread to shame. Over six Wednesday evenings in our newly refurbished teaching kitchen, Noriko Fairweather, who runs her own neighbourhood bakery, will guide you through basic white and wholemeal loaves, flatbreads, bread rolls and, in the final week, a sourdough made from a starter you will take home and keep alive yourself. Everything you bake goes home with you, so bring a large container or cloth bag each week. The course fee of £75 does not cover ingredients; instead, please pay £4 in cash to Noriko at the start of each session. Please note that, although no nuts are used in our recipes, the kitchen is shared with other classes and we cannot guarantee a nut-free environment. Aprons are provided; please tie back long hair.

D. Get More from Your Phone. Do you own a smartphone or tablet but use it for little more than calls? In this patient, unhurried course, Emeka Castellano and his team of volunteers will show you how to make video calls to family, take and share photographs, shop online safely and spot the warning signs of a scam message. The course runs for five weeks. Sessions take place in the college library on Monday evenings from 6 to 7.30 p.m., slightly earlier than most of our classes, so that learners can travel home before it gets too late. Please bring your own device, fully charged, along with any passwords you already use – written down if necessary. The course is free for anyone who lives in the borough; simply show proof of address, such as a recent utility bill, when you enrol. Others pay £30.

E. Watercolour for Beginners. Always wanted to paint but never known where to start? Artist Saoirse Patil will share her favourite techniques, from mixing colours and laying a flat wash to painting skies, trees and water. The course lasts eight weeks and meets on Thursday evenings in Studio 3 on the second floor. You will need paper, brushes and a small set of paints. If you would rather not buy these separately, a starter kit containing everything required can be bought from the college reception for £22. At the end of term, students are invited – though not obliged – to show one piece of work in a small exhibition in the college entrance hall. Fee: £85. Places on this popular course fill quickly, so early enrolment is advised.

sections.text:
Lifting and Screen Work: A Guide for Staff

A. Most people think of office work as low-risk, and compared with a building site or a warehouse it usually is. Yet the injuries that do occur in offices tend to build up slowly rather than happen in a single moment. Aching shoulders, a stiff lower back and tired eyes rarely send anyone to hospital, but they are among the commonest reasons staff here take time off. This guide explains what you can do yourself and what support the company provides. It was put together by our occupational health nurse, Farida Rahimi, with help from colleagues across the building.

B. Lifting is where office staff are most likely to hurt themselves suddenly. Boxes of printer paper, archive files and returned equipment are heavier than they look, and people often grab them in a hurry. Before you lift anything, test the weight by tipping one corner. If you cannot raise it comfortably, do not attempt to carry it alone. Keep the load close to your waist, bend at the knees rather than the hips, and avoid twisting your body while you hold it; turn by moving your feet instead. Bruno Esposito, our facilities manager, points out that two trolleys are kept beside the post room on every floor, and that staff should book them rather than carry stock up the stairs. He has also asked suppliers to deliver paper in smaller packs, so nobody needs to lift a full carton.

C. If something is too heavy, ask for help or report it. Rafael Takahashi, the staff health and safety representative, says many employees worry that asking for assistance will make them look weak or slow. "The opposite is true," he says. "Someone who stops to get a second pair of hands is doing their job properly." He adds that any strain or near miss should be recorded in the incident book at reception, even if you feel fine afterwards, because a pattern of small reports often reveals a problem with how a task is organised.

D. Screen work causes discomfort in a quieter way. Sitting in one position for hours places constant pressure on the same muscles, and the effects may not appear for weeks. The top of your monitor should be roughly level with your eyes, and the screen about an arm's length away. Your feet should rest flat on the floor or on a footrest, and your forearms should be roughly horizontal when you type. Laptops are a particular concern: because the screen and keyboard are joined, it is impossible to set both at the right height. Bruno Esposito's team will supply a separate keyboard and a stand to anyone using a laptop for more than an hour a day.

E. Changing position matters at least as much as perfect posture. Physiotherapist Akosua Brandt studied sixty staff at a regional call centre over six months. Those who stood up or walked for a few minutes every half hour reported noticeably less neck and back pain than those who took a single long break at lunch, even though both groups spent similar total time away from their desks. Brandt is careful to say that her study was small and that the workers knew they were being observed, so the result should not be treated as final. Even so, she recommends short, frequent breaks over occasional long ones.

F. Your eyes need attention too. Ioana Delacroix, an optometrist who visits the office twice a year, explains that staring at a screen reduces how often we blink, which leaves the eyes dry and sore. She suggests looking at something across the room from time to time to let the focusing muscles relax. She also stresses that screen work does not damage eyesight permanently, but it can reveal an existing problem that a person had not noticed. Anyone who uses a screen regularly is entitled to an eye test paid for by the company, and if you need glasses specifically for screen work, the company will contribute towards their cost.

G. Finally, every new member of staff must complete a workstation assessment within their first fortnight. The form takes about fifteen minutes and is reviewed by Farida Rahimi, who may arrange a desk visit if anything looks wrong. You should repeat the assessment whenever you move desks or your duties change significantly. Rahimi admits that many people treat the form as a box-ticking exercise, but she says the honest answers are what allow her team to fix problems before they turn into injuries.

questions.prompt: Before picking anything up, staff should check how heavy it is by tilting one ______.
questions.evidence: test the weight by tipping one corner

explanation.en: Paragraph B tells staff to test the weight by tipping one corner. 'Tilting' in the summary means the same as 'tipping'.
explanation.ru: В абзаце B сотрудникам советуют проверить вес, наклонив один угол ("tipping one corner"). Слово "Tilting" в пересказе означает то же, что "tipping".
explanation.uk: В абзаці B працівникам радять перевірити вагу, нахиливши один кут ("tipping one corner"). Слово "Tilting" у переказі означає те саме, що "tipping".

questions.prompt: While an item is being carried, the load should be held near the ______.
questions.evidence: Keep the load close to your waist

explanation.en: Paragraph B says to keep the load close to your waist. 'Held near' restates 'close to'.
explanation.ru: В абзаце B сказано, что груз нужно держать близко к поясу ("waist"). "Held near" передаёт тот же смысл, что "close to".
explanation.uk: В абзаці B сказано, що вантаж треба тримати близько до пояса ("waist"). "Held near" передає той самий зміст, що й "close to".

questions.prompt: To change direction while holding something, staff should use their ______ rather than twist their body.
questions.evidence: turn by moving your feet instead

explanation.en: Paragraph B warns against twisting and says to turn by moving your feet instead. 'Knees' is wrong because the knees are for bending, not for turning.
explanation.ru: Абзац B предостерегает от скручивания корпуса и советует вместо этого поворачиваться, переступая ногами ("feet"). Вариант "Knees" неверен: колени нужны, чтобы сгибаться, а не чтобы поворачиваться.
explanation.uk: Абзац B застерігає від скручування корпусу й радить натомість повертатися, переступаючи ногами ("feet"). Варіант "Knees" неправильний: коліна потрібні, щоб згинатися, а не щоб повертатися.

questions.prompt: Trolleys that staff can book are kept next to the ______ on each floor.
questions.evidence: two trolleys are kept beside the post room on every floor

explanation.en: In Paragraph B the facilities manager says the trolleys are kept beside the post room on every floor. 'Next to' means 'beside'.
explanation.ru: В абзаце B завхоз говорит, что тележки стоят рядом с почтовой комнатой ("post room") на каждом этаже. "Next to" означает "beside".
explanation.uk: В абзаці B завгосп каже, що візки стоять поруч із поштовою кімнатою ("post room") на кожному поверсі. "Next to" означає "beside".

questions.prompt: Even a minor strain that seems to cause no harm should be noted in the ______ at reception.
questions.evidence: should be recorded in the incident book at reception

explanation.en: Paragraph C says any strain or near miss should be recorded in the incident book at reception, even if you feel fine afterwards.
explanation.ru: В абзаце C сказано, что любое растяжение или случай, когда травма едва не произошла, нужно записывать в журнал происшествий ("incident book") на стойке регистрации ("reception"), даже если потом вы чувствуете себя нормально.
explanation.uk: В абзаці C сказано, що будь-яке розтягнення чи випадок, коли травма ледь не сталася, треба записувати в журнал інцидентів ("incident book") на рецепції ("reception"), навіть якщо потім ви почуваєтеся добре.

questions.prompt: When typing, staff should keep their ______ more or less horizontal.
questions.evidence: your forearms should be roughly horizontal when you type

explanation.en: Paragraph D says your forearms should be roughly horizontal when you type. 'More or less' restates 'roughly'. The feet are also mentioned, but they should rest flat on the floor.
explanation.ru: В абзаце D сказано, что при наборе текста предплечья должны быть примерно горизонтальны ("horizontal"). "More or less" передаёт смысл "roughly". Ступни ("feet") тоже упоминаются, но они должны стоять ровно на полу.
explanation.uk: В абзаці D сказано, що під час набору тексту передпліччя мають бути приблизно горизонтальними ("horizontal"). "More or less" передає зміст "roughly". Ступні ("feet") теж згадуються, але вони мають рівно стояти на підлозі.

questions.evidence: Bruno Esposito's team will supply a separate keyboard and a stand to anyone using a laptop

explanation.en: Paragraph D says Bruno Esposito's team will supply a keyboard and a stand to anyone who uses a laptop for more than an hour a day.

explanation.uk: В абзаці D сказано, що команда Bruno Esposito видасть клавіатуру й підставку всім, хто працює за ноутбуком понад годину на день.

questions.evidence: the workers knew they were being observed, so the result should not be treated as final

explanation.en: In Paragraph E, Akosua Brandt says the workers in her study knew they were being observed, so the result should not be treated as final.
explanation.ru: В абзаце E Akosua Brandt говорит, что работники в её исследовании знали, что за ними наблюдают, поэтому результат не стоит считать окончательным.
explanation.uk: В абзаці E Akosua Brandt каже, що працівники в її дослідженні знали, що за ними спостерігають, тому результат не слід вважати остаточним.

questions.prompt: believes that small incidents should be written down even if nobody seems to be hurt
questions.evidence: any strain or near miss should be recorded in the incident book at reception, even if you feel fine afterwards

explanation.en: Paragraph C reports Rafael Takahashi's view that strains and near misses should be recorded even if you feel fine. The incident book is at reception, but the advice comes from Takahashi.
explanation.ru: В абзаце C приводится мнение Rafael Takahashi: растяжения и случаи, когда травма едва не произошла, нужно записывать, даже если вы чувствуете себя нормально. Журнал происшествий находится на стойке регистрации, но этот совет даёт именно Takahashi.
explanation.uk: В абзаці C наведено думку Rafael Takahashi: розтягнення й випадки, коли травма ледь не сталася, треба записувати, навіть якщо ви почуваєтеся добре. Журнал інцидентів лежить на рецепції, але цю пораду дає саме Takahashi.

sections.text:
What Our Animals Give Us

A. Walk down almost any residential street and you will pass evidence of a quiet devotion: a bag of dog biscuits in a shopping basket, a scratching post glimpsed through a window, a hutch at the bottom of a garden. In many wealthy countries, roughly half of all households now include at least one animal, and owners happily spend sums on food, toys and veterinary care that would have astonished their grandparents. Yet from a purely practical point of view, most modern pets do very little. They do not pull ploughs, guard grain or bring home dinner. So why do so many of us choose to share our homes with them?

B. Part of the answer lies in history. Dogs were the first animals to be domesticated, descending from wolves that began living alongside human groups at least 15,000 years ago. Those early dogs earned their place by helping with hunting and by warning of approaching danger. Cats arrived by a different route. When people began farming and storing grain, the stores attracted mice, and the mice attracted wild cats, which moved in of their own accord and appear to have largely domesticated themselves. For thousands of years, then, the relationship was essentially a working arrangement. Keeping animals mainly for company, rather than for the jobs they could do, became widespread only much later, largely within the last two centuries.

C. That shift makes more sense once you look at what happens inside us when we spend time with an animal. Researchers have found that when dogs and their owners gaze at each other, levels of oxytocin, a hormone linked to the bond between parents and babies, rise in both the human and the dog. In a smaller study of her own, the psychologist Dr Siobhan Kearney asked forty volunteers to complete a stressful arithmetic task and then spend ten minutes either sitting quietly or stroking a friendly cat. Those who had been with the cat reported feeling calmer afterwards, and their heart rates returned to normal more quickly. Kearney is careful not to overstate the result. 'It was one group of people in one laboratory,' she says. 'But it fits what owners have been telling us for years.'

D. Pets also reshape our days in ways we hardly notice. A dog needs walking whether or not its owner feels like going out, and studies have repeatedly found that dog owners are, on average, more physically active than people without dogs. Just as important, perhaps, is who they meet along the way. The sociologist Arjun Mehta spent a year interviewing dog walkers in three city parks and concluded that a dog works as what he calls a 'social passport'. Strangers who would never speak to a lone adult will happily stop to ask a dog's name or age, and many of Mehta's interviewees said they knew far more of their neighbours since getting a dog. Cat owners, he admits, were not part of the research.

E. For people living alone, these effects can matter a great deal. Rhys Abernathy, a retired engineer, adopted a former racing greyhound eighteen months after his wife died. 'I had stopped bothering with mealtimes, stopped bothering with most things,' he recalls. 'Suddenly there was someone who needed feeding at seven every morning.' He insists that the dog did not replace human company; instead, it got him out of the house, where human company could find him again.

F. Children are often given a pet in the hope that it will teach them responsibility and kindness. There is some evidence that looking after an animal helps young people understand that others have needs and feelings, although the research is more mixed than many parents assume. In practice, the daily work of feeding a rabbit and cleaning out its hutch frequently falls to adults once the novelty has worn off. That is worth remembering before anyone promises that a new pet will be entirely the child's responsibility.

G. None of this means that a pet is a cure for every difficulty, and it would be dishonest to pretend otherwise. Animals cost money, restrict holidays and can trigger allergies. Their lives are also far shorter than ours, so owners must expect, sooner or later, to grieve. Animal welfare charities report that some pets are handed back within months because their new owners underestimated the commitment involved. A pet chosen on impulse, to fill a gap that really calls for something else, may end up making both animal and owner unhappy.

H. Still, the appeal endures, and perhaps the simplest explanation is the best one. With other people we are always being judged, at least a little, on our looks, our success or our conversation. A dog waiting at the door or a cat settling on a lap asks for none of that. What pets offer, more than anything, is a kind of acceptance that is rare elsewhere in life, and for many owners that alone is worth every vet's bill.
sections.title: What Our Animals Give Us

questions.prompt: No animal was domesticated earlier than the dog.
questions.evidence: Dogs were the first animals to be domesticated

explanation.en: Paragraph B says dogs were the first animals to be domesticated, which means no other animal was domesticated before them.
explanation.ru: В абзаце B сказано, что собаки были первыми одомашненными животными. Значит, ни одно другое животное не было одомашнено раньше них.
explanation.uk: В абзаці B сказано, що собаки були першими одомашненими тваринами. Отже, жодну іншу тварину не одомашнили раніше за них.

questions.prompt: Early farmers brought wild cats onto their land to deal with mice.
questions.evidence: which moved in of their own accord and appear to have largely domesticated themselves

explanation.en: Paragraph B says the wild cats came by themselves because of the mice. People did not bring them in, so the statement contradicts the passage.
explanation.ru: В абзаце B сказано, что дикие кошки пришли сами, потому что их привлекали мыши. Люди их не приводили, так что утверждение противоречит тексту.
explanation.uk: В абзаці B сказано, що дикі коти прийшли самі, бо їх приваблювали миші. Люди їх не приводили, тож твердження суперечить тексту.

questions.prompt: When dogs and owners look at each other, oxytocin rises in the owners but not in the dogs.
questions.evidence: rise in both the human and the dog

explanation.en: Paragraph C says oxytocin levels go up in both the person and the dog, not only in the person.
explanation.ru: В абзаце C сказано, что уровень окситоцина повышается и у человека, и у собаки, а не только у человека.
explanation.uk: В абзаці C сказано, що рівень окситоцину підвищується і в людини, і в собаки, а не лише в людини.

questions.prompt: All of the volunteers in Kearney's study already owned cats.

explanation.en: Paragraph C says Kearney used forty volunteers and some of them stroked a cat. It never says whether any of them owned cats themselves.
explanation.ru: В абзаце C сказано, что Kearney провела эксперимент с сорока добровольцами и некоторые из них гладили кошку. Но нигде не говорится, были ли у кого-то из них свои кошки.
explanation.uk: В абзаці C сказано, що Kearney провела експеримент із сорока добровольцями і дехто з них гладив кішку. Але ніде не сказано, чи мав хтось із них власних котів.

questions.prompt: Mehta carried out his interviews in more than one location.
questions.evidence: interviewing dog walkers in three city parks

explanation.en: Paragraph D says Mehta interviewed dog walkers in three different parks, so his research took place in more than one place.
explanation.ru: В абзаце D сказано, что Mehta опрашивал людей, гуляющих с собаками, в трёх разных парках. Значит, его исследование проводилось не в одном месте.
explanation.uk: В абзаці D сказано, що Mehta опитував людей, які вигулювали собак, у трьох різних парках. Отже, його дослідження проводилося не в одному місці.

questions.prompt: Abernathy's greyhound had a successful career as a racing dog.

explanation.en: Paragraph E says the greyhound used to be a racing dog. It says nothing about whether it won races or did well, so we cannot know.
explanation.ru: В абзаце E сказано, что грейхаунд раньше был беговой собакой. Но о том, выигрывал ли он забеги или хорошо выступал, ничего не говорится, поэтому мы не можем этого знать.
explanation.uk: В абзаці E сказано, що грейгаунд раніше був біговим собакою. Але про те, чи вигравав він перегони або чи добре виступав, нічого не сказано, тож ми не можемо цього знати.

groups.instruction: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage? Write TRUE if the statement agrees with the information, FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, or NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.

questions.prompt: Which TWO of the following does the writer give as reasons why early dogs were valued?
questions.evidence: helping with hunting and by warning of approaching danger

explanation.en: Paragraph B says early dogs helped with hunting and warned of danger. Pulling ploughs and guarding grain appear in Paragraph A as jobs modern pets do not do, and catching mice is linked to cats, not dogs.
explanation.ru: В абзаце B сказано, что первые собаки помогали на охоте и предупреждали об опасности. Таскать плуг и охранять зерно — это работа из абзаца A, которую современные питомцы не выполняют, а ловля мышей связана с кошками, а не с собаками.
explanation.uk: В абзаці B сказано, що перші собаки допомагали на полюванні й попереджали про небезпеку. Тягнути плуг і охороняти зерно — це робота з абзацу A, яку сучасні улюбленці не виконують, а ловіння мишей пов’язане з котами, а не із собаками.

groups.instruction: Choose TWO correct answers for each question.

options.text: They did better on the arithmetic task.
They asked to spend longer with the cat.
Their oxytocin levels went up sharply.
They described themselves as more relaxed.
Their heart rates settled down sooner.

questions.prompt: Which TWO results does Kearney report for the volunteers who stroked a cat?
questions.evidence: reported feeling calmer afterwards, and their heart rates returned to normal more quickly

explanation.en: Paragraph C says these volunteers felt calmer and their heart rates returned to normal faster. Oxytocin is mentioned only in other research about dogs, and the arithmetic task was done before the cat, not measured afterwards.
explanation.ru: В абзаце C сказано, что эти добровольцы стали спокойнее, а их пульс быстрее вернулся к норме. Окситоцин упоминается только в другом исследовании — о собаках, а задание по арифметике давали до того, как гладили кошку, и после этого его результаты не измеряли.
explanation.uk: В абзаці C сказано, що ці добровольці стали спокійнішими, а їхній пульс швидше повернувся до норми. Окситоцин згадується лише в іншому дослідженні — про собак, а завдання з арифметики давали до того, як гладили кішку, і після цього його результати не вимірювали.

groups.instruction: Choose TWO correct answers for each question.

questions.prompt: Mehta says a dog functions as a ______, making it easier for its owner to chat with people they do not know.
questions.evidence: a dog works as what he calls a 'social passport'

explanation.en: Paragraph D says Mehta calls a dog a 'social passport' because strangers stop to talk to dog walkers.
explanation.ru: В абзаце D сказано, что Mehta называет собаку «social passport», потому что незнакомые люди останавливаются, чтобы поговорить с теми, кто гуляет с собакой.
explanation.uk: В абзаці D сказано, що Mehta називає собаку «social passport», бо незнайомці зупиняються, щоб поговорити з тими, хто вигулює собаку.

questions.prompt: After losing his wife, Abernathy had stopped paying attention to ______ and most other things.
questions.evidence: I had stopped bothering with mealtimes, stopped bothering with most things

explanation.en: In Paragraph E, Abernathy says he had stopped bothering with mealtimes; 'stopped paying attention to' restates 'stopped bothering with'.
explanation.ru: В абзаце E Abernathy говорит, что перестал следить за временем еды; «stopped paying attention to» — это перефразировка «stopped bothering with».
explanation.uk: В абзаці E Abernathy каже, що перестав стежити за часом їжі; «stopped paying attention to» — це перефразування «stopped bothering with».

questions.prompt: Besides being expensive and making holidays harder, pets can cause ______ in some people.
questions.evidence: Animals cost money, restrict holidays and can trigger allergies.

explanation.en: Paragraph G lists the costs of pets: money, limits on holidays and allergies. 'Cause' restates 'trigger'.
explanation.ru: В абзаце G перечислены минусы содержания питомцев: расходы, ограничения в поездках на отдых и аллергия. «Cause» — это перефразировка «trigger».
explanation.uk: В абзаці G перелічено мінуси утримання домашніх тварин: витрати, обмеження у відпустках і алергія. «Cause» — це перефразування «trigger».
